hints: Notice the boat moves at constant velocity $v$ while a constant drag force $F$ opposes the motion.
Recall that power is the rate of doing work against that drag force, so link work $Fx$ to time $t$ using $v = x/t$.
Check why no $\frac{1}{2}$ appears here: the $\frac{1}{2}$ is for kinetic energy, whereas this is steady working against a resistive force.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantities: speed $v$ is constant and the opposing drag force $F$ is constant.
At constant velocity the boat engine must provide a forward force equal in magnitude to $F$ to balance drag.
Recall power as rate of work done: $P = W/t$, with work $W = Fx$ for a constant force over distance $x$.
Substitute $W = Fx$ to get $P = Fx/t$, and use $x/t = v$ for constant speed.
This gives $P = Fv$, with unit $\text{N m s}^{-1} = \text{W}$. This is option B.

options.A: The factor $\frac{1}{2}$ belongs to kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$, not to power against a constant force.
options.B: Power to overcome drag is $P = Fv$ when force $F$ acts in the opposite direction to velocity $v$.
options.C: $\frac{1}{2}Fv^2$ is incorrect in both factor and units, since $F$ times $v^2$ does not give watts.
options.D: $Fv^2$ has units of $\text{N m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, not power in $\text{W}$, and confuses power with another dependence on $v$.
